title: "Engineer Course"

anchor-sections: false

The engineer course is organized as eight complete Chapters. Chapters 1–4 are
the mainline path; Chapters 5–8 are optional continuations. Chapters 1–7 are
ordinary clean-kernel units; Chapter 8 deliberately uses two independent
kernels and one shared preserved workspace. The sixteen former Chapter URLs
now lead to short migration guides, not a second current course.

::: {.callout-warning title="Course candidate · CONVERGING" appearance="simple"}
The public authoring grammar, Parameter System, and certified diagram scopes
remain `CONVERGING`; accepted numerical Results keep their existing meanings.
Generated figures are source-bound evidence for exact checkpoints, not proof
of course acceptance, release, or every historical cell. The website executes
no kernels or solvers.
:::

## Chapter 4 — Four-Port capstone

Rebuild the original physical four-Port probe circuit and inspect its
certified explicit composition. The required core reads the raw four-Port
feedline response, then applies PTC and retains the two feedline Ports for a
separately labeled response. Transform, one scalar response element, and
independent Direct and pump-off HB grids are optional continuations.

:::: {.card .course-card}
::: {.card-body}
### [Lesson 1 — Physical Plan](../examples/engineer/chapter-04/01-physical-plan.qmd) {.course-card-title .unlisted}
Declare the feedline, readout, floating branches, three couplers, and four
logical Ports without analysis-time rewiring.
:::
::::

:::: {.card .course-card}
::: {.card-body}
### [Lesson 2 — Explicit capstone](../examples/engineer/chapter-04/02-explicit-capstone.qmd) {.course-card-title .unlisted}
Apply the established explicit probe-tee composition and inspect its certified
authoring projection.
:::
::::

:::: {.card .course-card}
::: {.card-body}
### [Lesson 3 — PTC core](../examples/engineer/chapter-04/03-ptc-core.qmd) {.course-card-title .unlisted}
Read the raw four-Port feedline trace, compensate both probe Ports, retain the
feedline pair, and read the separately labeled three-sample PTC Direct S21
Result. This is the Chapter's core stopping point.
:::
::::

:::: {.card .course-card}
::: {.card-body}
### [Lessons 4–6 — Optional analysis](../examples/engineer/chapter-04/04-optional-transform.qmd) {.course-card-title .unlisted}
Continue with the same Plan through paired-coordinate transformation, a direct
6.2 GHz response-element lookup, and separate Direct and pump-off HB Results.
:::
::::

The [complete Chapter 4 source](../examples/engineer/chapter-04/chapter.qmd) is
the ordered aggregate. Download its
[zero-output Notebook](../examples/engineer/chapter-04/chapter.ipynb) and run

## Chapter 7 — Ordered multi-conductor RLGC

Author one ordered N=2 body with exact full RLGC matrices, eight finite pi
sections, and four 50 ohm signal Ports. Evaluate the baseline, 1.8 mm length,
and whole-C-matrix ×170/175 points on one three-frequency Direct request.

- [Lesson 1 — Ordered RLGC](../examples/engineer/chapter-07/01-rlgc.qmd)
- [Lesson 2 — Four signal Ports](../examples/engineer/chapter-07/02-ports.qmd)
- [Lesson 3 — Authoring and compiled diagrams](../examples/engineer/chapter-07/03-diagrams.qmd)
- [Lesson 4 — Parameter points](../examples/engineer/chapter-07/04-parameter-points.qmd)
- [Complete Chapter source](../examples/engineer/chapter-07/chapter.qmd) and
  [zero-output Notebook](../examples/engineer/chapter-07/chapter.ipynb)

The current deterministic renderer reports a typed fixed-connector collision
for the exact four-Port authoring layout. That presentation limitation does not
replace the model or its complete sixteen-channel Direct Result.

## Chapter 8 — Report and resolve

Persist Direct and loaded-root Results and build their report in one kernel.
Then start a second independent kernel, reconstruct the exact Plan/View/Spec in
the same preserved workspace, and call only `resolve()` for the root.

- [Lesson 1 — Persist Results](../examples/engineer/chapter-08/01-persist.qmd)
- [Lesson 2 — Restart and resolve](../examples/engineer/chapter-08/02-resolve.qmd)
- [Complete Chapter source](../examples/engineer/chapter-08/chapter.qmd) and
  [zero-output Notebook](../examples/engineer/chapter-08/chapter.ipynb)

## Eight-Chapter roadmap

| Chapter | Outcome | Availability |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Coupled grounded LC | Build, diagram, S11, loaded root, selected C | Current five-Lesson Chapter |
| 2. Sweep and Optimization | Inputs, bindings, points, spaces, and established Optimization workflow | Current four-Lesson Chapter |
| 3. CPW feedline/readout S21 | Ordered two-section CPW, coupled readout, two-Port response | Current three-Lesson Chapter; complete Default diagram reports a typed fixed-layout collision |
| 4. Four-Port capstone | Original physical Plan and PTC core, then optional transform, quantities, and pump-off HB | Current six-Lesson Chapter |
| 5. Library | Create, publish, instantiate, and reuse a Composite | Current three-Lesson Chapter |
| 6. Diagram customization | Default completion, bounded hints, composition, and A/B review | Current four-Lesson Chapter |
| 7. MTL | Ordered multi-conductor RLGC and finite-pi compiled evidence | Current four-Lesson Chapter; exact four-Port authoring layout reports a typed fixed-layout collision |
| 8. Report and resolve | Exact requests, Results, workspaces, reports, and restart-safe resolution | Current two-Lesson, two-kernel Chapter |

The [durable migration map](implementation/engineer-course-migration-map.qmd)
records how each former Chapter moves and which Concept, Contract, or
implementation page remains authoritative.

## Former Chapter URL guides

The sixteen prior QMD URLs remain as short no-code
[migration guides](../examples/tutorials/01_author_primitive.qmd). Their
superseded executable bodies, Notebooks, and checkpoint figures remain
available in Git history rather than as a second current syllabus. The five
historical fixtures remain implementation-baseline evidence and are not
imported by the current Chapters.

For rationale, read [Concept](concepts/physical-authority-and-reusable-composition.qmd).
For exact signatures, equations, invariants, identities, and failure behavior,
use the [Contract map](contracts/index.qmd).
